title: Fernando Alda Lab
text:
Principal Investigator




Fernando is broadly interested in the processes that generate and maintain biological diversity across species and landscapes. His work examines the influence of ecological and geological factors on genetic variation and speciation, spanning levels from genomes to entire ecosystems.
See his CV for more information.





Lab Technician




Óscar is a MS in Genetics and Genomics. He is a lab technician and research assistant doing molecular work and metabarcoding data analysis.

Interested in joining the lab?
We are seeking motivated, collaborative, and dynamic individuals to join the lab, including postdoctoral researchers, graduate students (master’s or Ph.D.), and undergraduates. We welcome those interested in evolutionary biology, systematics, population genomics, and freshwater biodiversity.
If you are curious about these topics, have your own ideas, or want to propose a project, we encourage you to get in touch!

title: Fernando Alda Lab
text:
Past Lab Members

William Hanson-Regan
Master’s Student (2021–2023)




Will completed a MS studying the drivers of gut microbiome diversity and community structure among native and introduced minnows (genus Cyprinella) in the southeastern United States. He is currently a criminal defense consultant, specialized in genetics.





Sebastian Jimenez
Undergraduate Student (2022–2023)




Sebastian was an honors undergraduate student working on the characterization and phylogenetic inference of complete mitochondrial genomes of Congo River lamprologine cichlids. Sebastian is now a senior at the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga.





Taya de Blonk
Undergraduate Student (2020–2021)




Taya was an undergraduate student working on the phylogeography of stonerollers (Campostoma) across their distribution range from Mexico to New York. Taya is now a PhD student at North Carolina State University and the North Carolina Museum of Natural Science.

title: Fernando Alda Lab
text:
Research Interests

Our research seeks to understand the processes that generate and shape biodiversity, with a focus on the genomics and evolution of freshwater fishes. We integrate fieldwork, biological collections, phylogenomics, and population genomics to investigate biodiversity patterns and how ecological and geological processes interact to drive diversification across spatial and temporal scales.


We adopt comparative and integrative approaches across taxa, geographic regions, and evolutionary scales, combining genomic, ecological, and morphological data to link variation within populations to patterns of diversification across lineages. In doing so, we aim to understand not only how biodiversity originates, but also how species adapt and respond to environmental change.

title: Fernando Alda Lab
text:
Main Research Lines



Genomic Diversity and Fish Evolution

We investigate genetic and genomic diversity of freshwater fishes to uncover evolutionary history and trait evolution across rapid radiations. Read more »




Phylogenomics: Data, Methods, and Inference

We develop and evaluate methods for genome-scale inference of species relationships, testing how different data types affect evolutionary hypotheses. Read more »




Biodiversity, Invasions, and Conservation

We study how genetic diversity, ecological interactions,and human activities shape biodiversity, including the role of invasive species and microbiomes. Read more »
